summary: Louis de La Vallée Poussin was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Liège, KU Leuven, the Sorbonne, and Leiden, he studied under Lévi and Kern, among others. He was a professor at Ghent University (1893–1929).

Louis-Mathieu Langlès worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Sinology. A student of Silvestre de Sacy at the Collège de France, he served as keeper at the Bibliothèque nationale and administrator-professor of Persian at INALCO from 1795 to 1824.

Louise Allison Cort is a scholar of Japanology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Simmons University and St Hugh's College before serving as ceramics curator at the Freer and Sackler Galleries of the Smithsonian Institution from 1981 to 2020.

Louise Child specializes in religious studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Leeds under Linda Hogan, also studying under Ringu Tulku, and later held a teaching post at the University of Leeds.

Loukram Ibempishak Devi is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Gauhati University (attested 1999) under the supervision of Sibnath Sarma, having also studied under S. Shyamkishore Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh.

Lourens P. van den Bosch is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Utrecht University between approximately 1970 and 1978 under Jan Gonda, and also studied with Th. P. van Baaren and others.
Lozang Samten studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.
Lozang Tenpa studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.
Luboš Bělka is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Masaryk University from 1978 to 1983 and held an academic post there around 1993.
Luca Brigada Villa is a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and computational fields. He has held academic posts at the University of Bergamo and the University of Pavia.

Luca Maria Olivieri is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who earned his doctorate at the Free University of Berlin. He directed the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East and was an associate professor at Ca' Foscari (2020–2021).

Lucia Dolce works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She served as Lecturer in Japanese Religions (attested 2003–2007) and associate professor (attested 2015) at SOAS University of London, and as a visiting member at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Lucia Galli is a scholar of Tibetology who completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford and held a post there.

Lucian Scherman was an Indologist who studied at Breslau and Munich under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Ernst Kuhn. He served as a professor at the University of Munich (~1901–1933) and curator/director at Museum Fünf Kontinente from 1907.

Luciano Petech was a scholar of Tibetology and history who studied under Giuseppe Tucci. He was a lector at the University of Allahabad (1938–1946) and held the Chair of History of Eastern Asia at Sapienza University of Rome (1955–1984).

Lucien Lévy-Bruhl was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and the Sorbonne. He held a post at the University of Paris (~1899–1927) and founded the Institut d'ethnologie.

Lucien Tesnière was a linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet and at Paris, Leipzig, and ENLOV. He held academic posts at the University of Ljubljana (~1921–1924), University of Strasbourg (1924–1937), and University of Montpellier (1937).
Lucy Annette Jones is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Rice University under the supervision of Anne Carolyn Klein and Edith Wyschogrod.

Ludo Rocher was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Ghent University and SOAS. He was Professor of Comparative Philology and Sanskrit at Université libre de Bruxelles (1959–1967) and later served as professor and chair at the University of Pennsylvania.

Ludwig Alsdorf was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at Hamburg under Walther Schubring and habilitation under Heinrich Lüders. He held posts at Berlin, Münster, and Allahabad, before succeeding Schubring as professor at Hamburg (1950–1972).
